content: Highland Spring is the second-largest provider of bottled water in the United Kingdom. The company produces both still and sparkling water at its manufacturing facility located in Blackford, Perth and Kinross, Scotland. Despite the brand's name, this area is not geographically part of the Scottish Highlands. In 2005, Highland Spring was the best-selling sparkling water in the UK. The water originates from two distinct sources, which the company has designated as HS1 and HS2. These two sources exhibit slight differences in their mineral composition and pH levels. Highland Spring was officially recognized as Natural Mineral Water in 1985. The water is extracted from a protected underground source located in the Ochil Hills. Within the 2,000-acre (approximately 8 square kilometers) catchment area, strict environmental controls are in place. Activities such as farming, agricultural spraying, construction, or habitation are strictly prohibited. The land surrounding the water source has been maintained free of pesticides and pollution for over two decades. This commitment to environmental preservation allowed Highland Spring to become the first British brand of Natural Mineral Water to achieve organic certification for its catchment area. The company is owned by Mahdi Al Tajir, a billionaire businessman from the United Arab Emirates.
